chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: The band argues; Danny refuses the part
summary: Danny's colleagues urged him to take it for extra pay, but Smitty and Danny refused to play a swishing character.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So I had to go back there, and the cats was waitin'? Said, "What did she say?" I said, "She wants me to act like a morphodyte." I said "Morphodyte." That's the word... In New Orleans, we said "Morphodyte." "Morphodice."
For a gay, for a gay guy.
DANNY BARKER: Yeah. So they said, "Go on, man, that's a good chance. You'll get maybe a hundred dollars more, man. You'll be an actor." Slick Jones said... I mean, Smitty
said, 'Man, I wouldn't play no part like that.'

He said, 'Man, I wouldn't play no part like that. In case your people come up to see you on the stage and you're out there swishin' like some woman, man.' He said, 'Man, I wouldn't do that.' He says, 'Suppose your relatives come.' They said, 'Oh, man, relatives. This is the stage.' They had a big argument. 'This is the stage. He's just an actor. You're just portraying a character. You ain't...' Smitty said, 'I wouldn't care what it is.' He said, 'I'd be a lover, but I ain't gonna be no goddamn morphodyte on the stage.'

So Miss Burgorne(?) said, 'Did you come to the decision, Danny?' I said, 'No, Miss Burgorne(?), I ain't gonna play that part.' She said, 'Oh, that was the chance for you. You don't get a chance but once in a lifetime. You could be in the Theatre.' So that killed that.
